marks.reason: Every language rejects 2^63 with out_of_range_integer at the same path, but the error names the range the language holds: 64 bits in Rust and Go, 2^53 - 1 in TypeScript.
Every language rejects -2^63 - 1 with out_of_range_integer at the same path, but the error names the range the language holds: 64 bits in Rust and Go, 2^53 - 1 in TypeScript.
A TypeScript number holds integers exactly only up to 2^53 - 1, where Rust and Go hold 64 bits. TypeScript rejects 2^53 + 1 with out_of_range_integer rather than round it.
A TypeScript number holds integers exactly only up to 2^53 - 1, where Rust and Go hold 64 bits. TypeScript rejects 2^63 - 1 with out_of_range_integer rather than round it.
A TypeScript number holds integers exactly only down to -(2^53 - 1), where Rust and Go hold 64 bits. TypeScript rejects -2^63 with out_of_range_integer rather than round it.

Each language spells a decoded number its own way when it encodes it again: Rust writes 150.0, Go keeps 1.50E+2 as it was read, TypeScript writes 150. The value is the same, so the canonical bytes are.

Go's encoder escapes U+2028 and U+2029, so JavaScript that embeds the JSON in a script can't break, where Rust and TypeScript write the characters. Both are the same JSON string, so the canonical bytes are equal.
